### context: full
CAST + MACHINE COST INPUT RULES:
  Lines marked deterministic are computed from the measured geometry and will REPLACE whatever you return for them — restate them, do not re-derive them.
  materialId=mat-lm25  [aluminium gravity casting → mat-lm25 (A356 / LM25, the heat-treatable gravity / sand alloy — not a drawing callout) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  subtype=gravity  [gravity: medium-volume aluminium — gravity die casting gives denser, heat-treatable (T6) structure than HPDC for wheels/knuckles/pistons, with cheaper tooling than a pressure die [pressure-tight, tolerance class, safety-critical assumed — confirm before quoting] — deterministic, use verbatim]
  yieldFraction=0.6  [gravity aluminium yield band 0.5–0.7, midpoint (feeding scales with the alloy's shrinkage) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  netWeightKg=2.8  [1037 cm³ × 0.0027 kg/cm³ (aluminium, confirmed by engineer) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieMouldCostGBP=13627  [gravity toolmaker shop model: 194 toolroom hours + steel + bought-outs from a 288 cm² parting footprint, moderate (2 undercut face(s) ≈ 1 slide(s)); kernel face-count parametric said £26,400 (not used) — a quotation overrides this — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieMouldLife=50000  [gravity tool life band — deterministic, use verbatim]
  cycleTimeSandGravHr=0.08  [gravity cycle band — deterministic, use verbatim]
  labourId=lab-uk-foundry  [foundry operative on the moulding / die-casting line and at the fettling bench — deterministic, use verbatim]
  fettlingMinutes=2  [light fettling — gravity aluminium, 2.8 kg: gate / riser removal and grind at the foundry rate (engineering-typical minutes) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  heatTreatCostPerKg=1.1  [gravity aluminium is solution treated and aged, T6 — £1.1/kg (advisor rate) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  shotBlastCostPerPart=0.35  [gravity castings are blasted to remove sand / scale / flash — £0.35 a part (advisor rate, flat; a large casting runs more) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  impregnationCostPerPart=0  [not pressure-tight (or ferrous) — no impregnation — deterministic, use verbatim]
  ndtCostPerPart=0  [not safety-critical — no radiography — deterministic, use verbatim]
  machiningCycleTimeHr=0.268  [0.268 hr, inside the 0.296 hr near-net finish envelope — deterministic, use verbatim]
  machiningSetupTimeHr=3  [4 datum/fixture setup(s) of the split-3axis routing × 45 min — deterministic, use verbatim]
  machiningOperations=Milling — +Z (40 faces) 0.072 hr on mach-haas-vf2; Milling — -Z (30 faces) 0.054 hr on mach-haas-vf2; Milling — +X (20 faces) 0.036 hr on mach-haas-vf2; Drilling — 10 holes (10×Ø10.0×24) [geometry-measured] 0.105 hr on mach-drill  [sums to 0.268 hr of finish machining — deterministic, use verbatim]
  setupCount=4  [4 fixturing(s) of the split-3axis routing (3 approach direction(s) measured) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  machineId=mach-haas-vf2  [cost-ranked 2 routing(s): split-3axis £13.30 (3-direction split routing: mach-haas-vf2 £46/hr + mach-drill £31/hr, 4 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 5000 + 0.8 min handling per part per setup) vs consolidated-5axis £21.66 (single-setup 5-axis consolidation: mach-haas-umc500 £77/hr, 1 setup(s) × 45 min / batch 5000 + 0.8 min handling per part per setup) → split-3axis, £8.36/part cheaper than consolidated-5axis — deterministic, use verbatim]
